nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$ be ω-complete partial orders and let $f : \alpha \times \beta \to \gamma$ be a Scott-continuous map, that is, a map that is monotone and preserves suprema of ω-chains. Its currying is the Scott-continuous map from $\alpha$ to the ω-complete partial order of Scott-continuous maps $\beta \to \gamma$, ordered pointwise, that sends $a$ to the map $b \mapsto f(a, b)$.
nodes.title: Currying of Scott-continuous maps

nodes.summary: Let $D$ be an ω-complete partial order with a least element $\bot$, and let $f : D \to D$ be Scott-continuous, that is, monotone and preserving suprema of ω-chains. Then the least fixed point $\operatorname{lfp} f$ of $f$ satisfies $f(\operatorname{lfp} f) = \operatorname{lfp} f$.
nodes.title: The least fixed point is a fixed point

nodes.summary: Let $D$ be an ω-complete partial order with a least element $\bot$. The least-fixed-point operator, sending a Scott-continuous map $f : D \to D$ to its least fixed point $\operatorname{lfp} f$, bundled as a Scott-continuous map from the ω-complete partial order of Scott-continuous maps $D \to D$, ordered pointwise, to $D$.
nodes.title: The least-fixed-point operator as a Scott-continuous map

nodes.summary: Let $D$ be an ω-complete partial order with a least element $\bot$, let $f : D \to D$ be Scott-continuous, that is, monotone and preserving suprema of ω-chains, and let $\operatorname{lfp} f$ be the supremum of the Kleene chain $\bot \le f(\bot) \le f(f(\bot)) \le \cdots$. If $a \in D$ satisfies $f(a) \le a$, then $\operatorname{lfp} f \le a$.
nodes.title: The least fixed point lies below every prefixed point

nodes.summary: Let $D$ be an ω-complete partial order with a least element $\bot$. For a Scott-continuous map $f : D \to D$, that is, one that is monotone and preserves suprema of ω-chains, let $\operatorname{lfp} f$ be its least fixed point. The map $f \mapsto \operatorname{lfp} f$, from the ω-complete partial order of Scott-continuous maps $D \to D$, ordered pointwise, to $D$, is Scott-continuous.
nodes.title: Scott continuity of the least-fixed-point operator

nodes.summary: Let $D$ be an ω-complete partial order with a least element $\bot$, and let $f : D \to D$ be Scott-continuous, that is, monotone and preserving suprema of ω-chains. The least fixed point $\operatorname{lfp} f$ of $f$ is the supremum of the Kleene chain $\bot \le f(\bot) \le f(f(\bot)) \le \cdots$, whose $n$-th term is the $n$-fold iterate $f^n(\bot)$.
nodes.title: Least fixed point of a Scott-continuous map

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$ be ω-complete partial orders, and let $g$ be a map from $\alpha$ to the ω-complete partial order of Scott-continuous maps $\beta \to \gamma$, ordered pointwise. If for every $b \in \beta$ the map $a \mapsto g(a)(b)$ is Scott-continuous, then $g$ is Scott-continuous. Here a map is Scott-continuous when it is monotone and preserves suprema of ω-chains.
nodes.title: Scott continuity into a function space is checked pointwise
